toegepas.rede_vinder: A name is 'gekry' (received) for a reason; 'het sy naam omdat' reads slightly clipped and unidiomatic.
toegepas.fout: 'het sy naam omdat' is clipped; Afrikaans says a thing 'het sy naam gekry' for a reason
toegepas.rede_keurder: The fixed expression 'sy naam gekry' is the natural Afrikaans, and the sentence still says the same thing.

toegepas.rede_vinder: The sentence before has 'Klip' as subject, so 'sy' could be read as referring to the stone rather than the Stone Age; 'die' removes the ambiguity under a heading that already names the Stone Age.
toegepas.fout: 'sy' follows a sentence whose subject is 'Klip', so it can point to two antecedents
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'die drie dele' removes the pronoun ambiguity under a heading that already names the Stone Age, without moving the meaning.

vlae.blok: Klip, brons en yster / Die Steentydperk in drie dele
vlae.teks: In Suider-Afrika was daar egter nie 'n aparte Bronstydperk nie. ... In Suid-Afrika het die Vroeë Steentydperk sowat twee miljoen jaar gelede begin.
vlae.rede: The lesson uses 'Suider-Afrika' in one block and 'Suid-Afrika' in the next; probably deliberate (different regions), but a person or the fact check should confirm, since a language agent cannot choose without guessing the content.

laat_vaar_vorige.na: Van die oudste tot die jongste
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'van ... tot' with the articles is the natural Afrikaans form; 'van oudste na jongste' echoes English 'from oldest to youngest'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Van oudste na jongste' follows the natural Afrikaans ordering pattern (cf. 'van klein na groot'), so the change is lateral.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: die koms van boere met yster
laat_vaar_vorige.na: die koms van boere wat yster gebruik het
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'boere met yster' is compressed and can attach to the wrong phrase; a short relative clause is clearer for Grade 5.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Embedding 'wat yster gebruik het' before 'op hul eie manier bly leef' stacks verbs mid-sentence and makes it harder for a Grade 5 reader.
